children: Memory stocks are showing signs of renewed investor interest after a period of weaker momentum, with Goldman Sachs pointing to improving technical conditions across the group.
, the iShares MSCI South Korea ETF (EWY) and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) are among the securities displaying patterns that could signal a shift from recent consolidation.

The setup comes as positioning in the broader AI trade remains relatively light. Goldman's prime brokerage data put gross leverage among U.S. fundamental long/short hedge funds at the 27th percentile of the past year, while net leverage was at the fourth percentile.
Options activity has also cooled. The CBOE Semiconductor ETF Volatility Index had dropped to about 36 from roughly 65 in July, indicating a substantial decline in expected price swings.

Goldman also noted that its technology long/short momentum basket has fallen about 50% from its late-June peak despite a recent rebound. South Korean equities could offer another catalyst, as recent flows have been driven by corporate buybacks while other investor groups have remained net sellers.

title: Micron and Sandisk Soar as Goldman Sees New Memory Stock Rally
